summary: Versioned file memory can become a slow, privacy-sensitive archive whose apparent auditability exceeds its actual correctness.

points.text: Append-only growth increases noise and retrieval collisions. Without compaction, expiry, and successor-aware ranking, stale statements remain easy for an agent to surface.

Git history conflicts with deletion obligations and secret remediation because content persists in repository history and clones. Sensitive or regulated memory may require a store with enforceable retention and erasure.
Human-readable files and indexes can diverge under concurrent writes or partial updates. A transactional database may provide stronger uniqueness, locking, and referential integrity.
Auditability does not validate truth. An incorrect model-generated inference can be perfectly versioned and repeatedly retrieved unless sources, confidence, and approval state are represented.
